title: Why "Break a Leg" Means Good Luck?! 4 Crazy English Idioms Native Speakers Actually Use | English Podcast

subtitles.en:
Hello everyone! Welcome back to the AB
English Podcast... I'm Mia!
subtitles.zh: 哈囉大家！歡迎回到 AB 英文播客節目，我是 Mia！

subtitles.en:
And I'm Alex! Oh, it's so great to be back
with you all today.
subtitles.zh: 我是 Alex！今天能再次跟大家空中相會真是太棒了。

subtitles.en:
Alex, you won't believe it... I had the most
awkward moment at work yesterday.
subtitles.zh: Alex 你絕對不敢相信……我昨天在公司經歷了超級尷尬的一刻。

subtitles.en:
Oh no! Another awkward Mia story? Come on,
tell me what happened!
subtitles.zh: 噢不！又有 Mia 的糗事可以聽了嗎？快點，快跟我說發生了什麼事！

subtitles.en:
Well, right at five PM, my American boss
smiled and said, 'Mia... let's call it a
day!'
subtitles.zh:
嗯，就在下午五點整，我的美國老闆笑咪咪地對我說：「Mia……今天就到此
為止吧！」

subtitles.en:
Haha, and what on earth did you think that
meant?
subtitles.zh: 哈哈，那你當時到底以為是什麼意思？

subtitles.en:
I thought... well, I thought he wanted to
name the day after me, or hang out all day!
subtitles.zh:
我以為……哎，我以為他要把這一天用我的名字命名，
或是要跟我混上一整天呢！

subtitles.en:
Oh Mia... 'Call it a day' just means—let's
stop working and head home!
subtitles.zh: 噢 Mia……那句話單純只是代表「收工下班、打道回府」啦！

subtitles.en:
Exactly! In English, you can know every
single word... but together? They mean
something totally unexpected.
subtitles.zh:
可不是嗎！在英文裡，你可能每個單字都認得……但湊在一起時，
意思卻完全出乎意料。

subtitles.en:
Hmm, linguists call that 'cognitive
contrast'—the gap between literal words and
real meaning.
subtitles.zh:
嗯，語言學家把這種現象稱為「認知衝突」——也就是字面含意與真正語意之間
的鴻溝。

subtitles.en:
Right! Just like our recent Short about 'Tell
me about it'—which actually means 'I agree,'
not 'Tell me a story!'
subtitles.zh:
沒錯！就像我們最近發布的短影音裡提到的那句話，
意思是「我深有同感」，而不是叫你「講個故事來聽聽」！

subtitles.en:
Exactly! Today, we're breaking down four
crazy idioms native speakers use every day...
so you'll never get confused again!
subtitles.zh:
沒錯！今天我們就要來拆解四個母語人士天天都在講的超反直覺慣用語……讓大
家以後再也不會搞得一頭霧水！

subtitles.en:
Alright, let's start with idiom number one:
'Break a leg!'
subtitles.zh: 好啦，我們就從第一個慣用語開始吧：「祝你好運」！

subtitles.en:
Imagine this... you're backstage, about to
give a huge presentation, and your hands are
shaking.
subtitles.zh:
想像一下這個畫面……你正待在後台，準備上台做一場重大簡報，
雙手緊張得止不住顫抖。

subtitles.en: Ugh, wow... I'd be completely terrified!
subtitles.zh: 呃，光想就可怕……我一定會嚇到魂飛魄散！

subtitles.en:
Then, your American coworker slaps your back
and yells: 'Hey Mia, break a leg out there!'
subtitles.zh:
這時候，你的美國同事用力拍了一下你的背大喊：「嘿 Mia，
摔斷一條腿吧！」

subtitles.en:
Wait... break a leg?! Why on earth would they
wish I break a bone?!
subtitles.zh: 等等……摔斷一條腿？！到底為什麼要詛咒我骨折受傷啊？！

subtitles.en:
Haha! Well, 'Break a leg' actually means
'Good luck' or 'Go do a fantastic job!'
subtitles.zh: 哈哈！哎呀，那句話其實代表「祝你好運」或是「祝你演出大成功」！

subtitles.en:
But... how does breaking a leg equal good
luck? That sounds absolutely crazy!
subtitles.zh: 可是……摔斷腿怎麼會等同於祝你好運呢？這聽起來也太瘋狂了吧！

subtitles.en:
It comes from an old theater superstition.
Actors used to believe theaters were full of
mischievous ghosts.
subtitles.zh:
這源自於以前劇院的迷信傳說。早期的演員相信劇院裡住著許多愛惡作劇的幽靈
鬼魂。

subtitles.en:
Ooh... ghosts who would ruin the whole show
if you dared to say 'Good luck'?
subtitles.zh:
喔……所以要是你敢說出「祝你好運」，那些鬼怪就會故意出來把整場演出搞砸
囉？

subtitles.en:
Exactly! So performers wished for the
opposite—just to fool the spirits.
subtitles.zh: 一點也沒錯！所以表演者才會故意講反話——就為了把那些惡靈給矇騙過去。

subtitles.en:
Wow, reverse psychology for theater ghosts!
So... can I say it before a big job
interview?
subtitles.zh:
哇，居然對劇院鬼怪使出逆向心理學！那……去參加重要的求職面試前也可以這
樣說嗎？

subtitles.en:
Definitely! Before any big speech, audition,
or exam... you can totally say, 'Break a
leg!'
subtitles.zh:
絕對可以！在任何重要演講、試鏡或是重大考試之前……你都可以對別人說這句
話祝他好運！

subtitles.en:
Hmm, and how do you reply when someone says
that to you?
subtitles.zh: 嗯，那要是別人對我說了這句話，我該怎麼回應呢？

subtitles.en: Just smile and say: 'Thank you! I will!'
subtitles.zh: 只要面帶微笑回答：「謝謝你！我會全力以赴的！」這樣就行了。

subtitles.en:
Ah, simple and sweet. No broken bones
required!
subtitles.zh: 啊，簡單又貼心，完全不需要真的跑去摔斷骨頭！

subtitles.en:
Now, onto idiom number two... 'Under the
weather.'
subtitles.zh: 現在，我們要進入第二個慣用語了……那就是「身體微恙」。

subtitles.en:
Ring, ring! Alex... you're not at the studio
today. Where are you?
subtitles.zh: 鈴鈴鈴！Alex……你今天怎麼沒出現在錄音室？你人到底在哪裡呀？

subtitles.en:
*Cough* Hey Mia... sorry, I can't make it
today. I'm feeling a bit under the weather.
subtitles.zh: 咳咳……嘿 Mia……抱歉，我今天去不了了。我感覺身體有點不大舒服。

subtitles.en:
Under the weather? But... aren't we all under
the weather? The sky is literally above
everyone!
subtitles.zh:
在天氣下面？可是……我們大家不都待在天氣下面嗎？
天空本來就罩在每個人頭頂上啊！

subtitles.en:
Haha, well yes, but 'under the weather' means
feeling slightly sick or unwell.
subtitles.zh: 哈哈，話是沒錯啦，但這個片語真正的意思是指微恙、身體不太舒服。

subtitles.en:
Ah! So like a mild headache or a cold... not
a major hospital emergency?
subtitles.zh: 啊！所以是指像輕微頭痛或小感冒那樣……而不是需要緊急送醫的那種重病囉？

subtitles.en:
Exactly. It's perfect for low energy, sore
throats, or the sniffles.
subtitles.zh: 沒錯。這很適合用在精神不濟、喉嚨痛或是流鼻水的時候。

subtitles.en:
Hmm, where did this sailing-sounding phrase
come from anyway?
subtitles.zh: 嗯，話說回來，這個聽起來很有航海氣息的片語到底打哪來的？

subtitles.en:
It really is from sailing! During bad ocean
storms, seasick sailors were sent below deck.
subtitles.zh:
它真的就是源自於航海！在海上遇到狂風暴雨時，
暈船的水手都會被送到甲板下方去歇息。

subtitles.en:
Oh! Beneath the ship's rail... sheltered from
the storm!
subtitles.zh: 噢！就是躲在船欄下方……避開外頭的暴風雨！

subtitles.en:
Right! They were literally resting 'under the
adverse weather.'
subtitles.zh: 對！他們字面上就是躲在「惡劣的天候底下」休養生息。

subtitles.en:
Wow, that's brilliant! It's such a polite,
professional way to call in sick to your
boss.
subtitles.zh: 哇，太妙了！這真的是跟老闆請病假時最得體、最有禮貌的說法呢。

subtitles.en:
Yes! You can simply say: 'I'm feeling a bit
under the weather today, so I'll be resting
at home.'
subtitles.zh:
沒錯！你可以直接這樣說：「我今天身體有點不太舒服，
會留在家裡好好休息。」

subtitles.en:
Oh, and you can use it to politely skip a
party too... right?
subtitles.zh: 噢，而且這也能用來禮貌婉拒聚會邀約對吧？

subtitles.en:
Absolutely! You can just say—'Thanks for the
invite, but I'm under the weather tonight!'
subtitles.zh:
完全可以！你可以直接說：『謝謝你的邀請，但我今晚身體有點微恙，
去不了了！』

subtitles.en:
Wow, now... idiom number three sounds pretty
hardcore: 'Bite the bullet!'
subtitles.zh: 哇，那……第三個片語聽起來超硬派的：『咬緊牙關』！

subtitles.en:
Yes! So, what's your mental image when you
hear 'bite the bullet'?
subtitles.zh: 沒錯！那當你聽到『咬子彈』時，腦中浮現什麼畫面？

subtitles.en:
Hmm... an action hero biting on real metal
bullets in an action movie!
subtitles.zh: 嗯……動作片英雄在電影裡狠咬金屬子彈的畫面！

subtitles.en:
Haha, well... it actually means forcing
yourself to do something unpleasant—something
you've been avoiding.
subtitles.zh: 哈哈，嗯……其實它是指硬著頭皮去面對某件你一直在逃避的苦差事。

subtitles.en:
Ah, like going to the dentist when you're
terrified of that drill?
subtitles.zh: 啊，就像明明怕死電鑽聲，卻還是不得不去看牙醫那樣？

subtitles.en:
Exactly! You totally dread it... but you just
have to bite the bullet and go.
subtitles.zh: 沒錯！你怕得要死……但終究得咬緊牙關硬著頭皮去。

subtitles.en:
Wait... did soldiers actually bite real
bullets back in the day?
subtitles.zh: 等等……以前的士兵真的會去咬真正的子彈嗎？

subtitles.en:
Sadly, yes. You see... before modern
anesthesia, battlefield surgery was brutally
painful.
subtitles.zh:
令人難過的是，真的會。你看……在現代麻醉技術發明前，
戰場上的手術簡直痛如凌遲。

subtitles.en: Oh no... zero pain relief during surgery?!
subtitles.zh: 天啊……手術全程完全沒有任何止痛藥？！

subtitles.en:
None at all. Doctors gave soldiers a soft
lead bullet to bite hard—so they wouldn't
scream, or bite through their own tongue.
subtitles.zh:
完全沒有。軍醫會給傷兵一顆較軟的鉛彈咬緊——這樣他們才不會痛到尖叫，
或是咬斷自己的舌頭。

subtitles.en:
Ugh, that gives me chills... But well, it
definitely makes the idiom impossible to
forget!
subtitles.zh: 呃，聽得我毛骨悚然……不過這下子真的徹底記住這個片語了！

subtitles.en:
Exactly. Today, it simply means finding the
courage to face an inevitable challenge.
subtitles.zh: 沒錯。在今天，它單純指鼓起勇氣，去面對避無可避的難關。

subtitles.en:
Like... finally doing your taxes right before
the deadline!
subtitles.zh: 就像……在最後截止日前硬著頭皮把稅給報完！

subtitles.en:
Exactly. Or finally having a serious talk
with your landlord or boss—like, 'I really
need to bite the bullet and ask for a raise.'
subtitles.zh:
沒錯。或是終於下定決心跟房東或老闆好好談判——像是：『我真的該咬緊牙關
去爭取加薪了。』

subtitles.en:
Whew... biting the bullet takes real courage,
but it feels so good once it's done!
subtitles.zh: 呼……咬緊牙關確實需要莫大勇氣，但一旦完成後真的通體舒暢！

subtitles.en:
And now... for our fourth idiom pair: 'Piece
of cake' and 'No sweat!'
subtitles.zh: 接下來……是我們的第四組片語：『小菜一碟』和『小意思、沒問題』！

subtitles.en:
Ooh, piece of cake! Wait... are we talking
about chocolate dessert?
subtitles.zh: 喔！一塊蛋糕！等等……我們是在討論巧克力甜點嗎？

subtitles.en:
Haha, well, not quite. Remember when your
laptop crashed yesterday... and just wouldn't
turn on?
subtitles.zh: 哈哈，那倒不是。還記得你昨天筆電當機……怎麼開都開不了嗎？

subtitles.en:
Oh, I almost cried! I honestly thought all
our recording files were lost forever!
subtitles.zh: 噢，我當時快哭出來了！我真的以為我們所有的錄音檔案全都化為烏有了！

subtitles.en:
And then... I pressed three shortcut keys,
restarted the system, and fixed it in five
seconds flat.
subtitles.zh: 然後呢……我按了三個快捷鍵、重啟系統，五秒鐘就徹底搞定。

subtitles.en:
I wanted to treat you to a nice steak dinner,
but you just smiled and said—'It was a piece
of cake! No sweat!'
subtitles.zh: 我原本想請你吃頓頂級牛排大餐，你卻只是笑著說：『小事一樁！小意思啦！』

subtitles.en:
So... what do you think those two phrases
actually mean?
subtitles.zh: 那麼……你覺得這兩句話到底是什麼意思呢？

subtitles.en:
Well, 'piece of cake' means something is
super easy—just as effortless as eating a
delicious slice of cake!
subtitles.zh:
嗯，『小菜一碟』是指某件事超級簡單——就跟吃下一塊美味的蛋糕一樣毫不費
力！

subtitles.en:
Spot on! And 'no sweat' means it required
zero hard effort—basically, 'No problem at
all!'
subtitles.zh:
完全沒錯！而『沒流汗』意思是不費吹灰之力——基本上就是『完全沒問題、
小意思』！

subtitles.en:
Hmm, can you say 'piece of cake' about school
exams?
subtitles.zh: 嗯，那學校考試也可以用『小菜一碟』來形容嗎？

subtitles.en:
Definitely! Like: 'How was the English
test?'—'Oh, piece of cake! I totally aced
it!'
subtitles.zh:
當然可以！例如：『英文考得怎麼樣？』——『噢，
小菜一碟！我直接拿滿分！』

subtitles.en:
Ah! And when someone thanks you for carrying
heavy boxes, you can just say—'No sweat!'
subtitles.zh: 啊！當別人因為你幫忙搬重物而道謝時，你也可以瀟灑回一句：『小意思啦！』

subtitles.en:
Exactly! It sounds so much more natural and
relaxed than a stiff 'You're welcome.'
subtitles.zh: 沒錯！這比起生硬古板地說『不客氣』，聽起來自然又放鬆多了。

subtitles.en:
Wow, these two phrases really make you sound
so confident and easygoing.
subtitles.zh: 哇，這兩句話真的會讓人聽起來既自信又隨和。

subtitles.en:
They really do! Now... let's test our
listeners with a quick challenge!
subtitles.zh: 真的！現在……讓我們用一場快問快答來考驗一下聽眾朋友們吧！

subtitles.en:
Challenge time! Listeners, let's see if you
can pick the right idiom for each situation.
subtitles.zh: 挑戰時間到！聽眾朋友們，看看你們能不能在各個情境中選出最適當的片語。

subtitles.en:
Alright, question one: Your friend is walking
into a major job interview... What do you say
to them?
subtitles.zh:
好的，第一題：你的朋友即將走進一場至關重要的求職面試……這時你該對他說
什麼？

subtitles.en:
Hmm, do you tell them to 'Bite the bullet,'
or do you say 'Break a leg'?
subtitles.zh: 嗯，你是叫他『咬緊牙關』，還是祝他『演出順利、好運連連』呢？

subtitles.en:
The answer is—'Break a leg!' Wishing them the
best of luck to shine out there!
subtitles.zh: 答案是——『祝你大獲全勝、好運連連』！祝福他在面試舞台上大顯身手！

subtitles.en: Exactly! Now... lay question two on us, Alex!
subtitles.zh: 完全正確！現在……給我們第二題吧，Alex！

subtitles.en:
Question two: You wake up on Saturday with a
scratchy throat and a bad headache... Your
friend texts asking to hang out. What do you
reply?
subtitles.zh:
第二題：週六你起床發現喉嚨乾癢、頭痛欲裂……朋友傳訊約你出門鬼混。
這時你該怎麼回傳訊息？

subtitles.en:
Ah, you text back: 'Sorry, I'm feeling a bit
under the weather today... so I'm gonna
pass.'
subtitles.zh: 啊，你可以回訊說：『抱歉，我今天身體有點不太舒服……先不去了。』

subtitles.en:
Spot on! And now... get ready for our special
bonus callback to Short Number 4!
subtitles.zh: 完全正確！現在……準備迎接呼應我們第 4 部短影片的特別彩蛋題吧！

subtitles.en:
Imagine this... your coworker complains that
Monday morning traffic was an absolute
nightmare. And well, you were stuck in that
exact same traffic jam! So... what do you
say?
subtitles.zh:
想像一下這個情境……你的同事抱怨週一早上的交通簡直是場惡夢，
而你剛好也塞在同一個車陣裡！那麼……你會怎麼回答呢？

subtitles.en:
Hmm, do you ask for a thirty-minute detailed
explanation... or do you just say, 'Tell me
about it!'?
subtitles.zh: 嗯，你是會叫對方詳細交代半小時的細節……還是隨口回一句「可不是嘛！」？

subtitles.en:
Oh, you definitely say: 'Tell me about it!'
meaning, 'I totally agree!' And—haha—you
certainly don't start telling the story of
that red sedan!
subtitles.zh:
噢，你當然要說「可不是嘛！」，代表「我完全同意！
」而且——哈哈——千萬別開始講那輛紅色轎車的故事！

subtitles.en:
Haha, brilliant! You got a hundred percent on
that one!
subtitles.zh: 哈哈，太精采了！這題你拿了一百分！

subtitles.en:
Phew! Honestly, that test was a total piece
of cake!
subtitles.zh: 呼！說真的，剛才那道測驗簡直是小菜一碟！

subtitles.en: Haha, wow, nice usage right there!
subtitles.zh: 哈哈，哇，這個用法用得真漂亮！

subtitles.en:
Alright, let's do a quick thirty-second recap
of today's four key idioms!
subtitles.zh: 好啦，讓我們用短短三十秒快速複習今天學到的四個核心成語！

subtitles.en:
Number one: 'Break a leg'—which means wishing
someone good luck before a big performance.
subtitles.zh: 第一個：「祝你好運」，意思是重大演出前祝對方發揮順利。

subtitles.en:
Number two: 'Under the weather'—meaning
you're feeling slightly sick, tired, or just
unwell.
subtitles.zh: 第二個：「身體微恙」，代表你感覺有點感冒、不適或提不起精神。

subtitles.en:
Number three: 'Bite the bullet'—meaning you
find the courage to face a tough, inevitable
task.
subtitles.zh: 第三個：「咬緊牙關」，意思是鼓起勇氣去面對逃不掉的艱巨任務。

subtitles.en:
Number four: 'Piece of cake' and 'No
sweat'—meaning super easy, or 'you're very
welcome!'
subtitles.zh:
第四個：「易如反掌」以及「不客氣、小意思」，
表示事情輕而易舉，或是回答對方的感謝！

subtitles.en:
And our bonus phrase: 'Tell me about
it!'—meaning, 'I completely agree and I feel
your pain!'
subtitles.zh: 還有加碼的實用語：「可不是嘛！」，意思就是「我完全贊同，深有同感！」

subtitles.en:
And now, for our Question of the Day: What's
the most confusing English idiom you've ever
heard? Tell us down in the comments!
subtitles.zh:
接下來是我們今天的互動問題：你聽過最讓你滿頭霧水的英文成語是什麼呢？
快在下方留言告訴我們吧！

subtitles.en:
Remember, folks... listening is great, but
speaking is where real fluency truly happens.
subtitles.zh: 各位要記住……多聽很棒，但只有真正開口說，才能達到真正的流利。

subtitles.en:
Be sure to check our video description for
our two free GugoPro language learning tools!
subtitles.zh: 別忘了查看影片資訊欄，領取兩款免費的語言學習工具！

subtitles.en:
Yeah! You can practice listening with the
YouTube Dictation Player, and speak one-on-
one with our AI Speaking Tutor.
subtitles.zh:
沒錯！你可以使用聽寫播放器訓練聽力，還能跟人工智慧口說導師進行一對一對
話練習。

subtitles.en:
Both tools are completely free, so jump right
in and start practicing right now!
subtitles.zh: 這兩款工具都完全免費，快點去試試看，現在就開始練習吧！

subtitles.en:
If you learned something new today, please
hit that like button, subscribe, and share
this with a friend.
subtitles.zh: 如果你今天學到了新知識，請記得幫我們按讚、訂閱，並分享給身邊的朋友。

subtitles.en:
Thank you so much for joining us today. Keep
practicing, and we'll see you in the next
episode!
subtitles.zh: 非常感謝大家今天的收聽。繼續堅持練習，我們下一集再見囉！

subtitles.en: Take care, everyone! Bye-bye!
subtitles.zh: 大家保重！再見啦！
